speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To understand your frightening sleep episodes better, can you describe what happens right before or during the awakening? Also, do you snore or breathe very loudly while you sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you ever stop breathing or gasp for air during these episodes? REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography. REQUEST IMAGES: Sleep_study_results.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the sleep study is normal and she isn't gasping for air, these frightening episodes sound like night terrors rather than apnea. Do you notice if she has any physical twitching or stiffening of her muscles during these events? Also, does she have any history of head injuries or family members with similar sleep behaviors?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.
